description.short_caption: Immunofluorescent stain showing deposition along the dermoepidermal junction.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an immunofluorescent stain of skin tissue, highlighting a bright green fluorescence pattern along the dermoepidermal junction. The fluorescence is linear and continuous, suggesting deposition of immune complexes or antibodies. The epidermis is visible above the junction, with the dermis below. The staining technique emphasizes specific antigen-antibody interactions.
visible_findings: linear green fluorescence at the dermoepidermal junction
epidermis above and dermis below the junction

description.short_caption: Histopathology of skin showing epidermal necrosis and subepidermal blister formation.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a section of skin stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The epidermis exhibits necrosis and detachment from the underlying dermis, forming a subepidermal blister. The dermis shows inflammatory infiltrates, with evidence of edema and possible fibrin deposition. The findings are consistent with a blistering skin disorder, potentially of infectious or autoimmune etiology.
